correctness.rationale: In the pure binary relation graph of one bijection, FO1 tests only existence of fixed and nonfixed vertices, yielding three nonempty-domain classes. FO2 can define F, T (2-cycle points), and L (>=3-cycle points). The permanent 2-pebble game sees first two cycle multiplicities clipped at 2 and whether L is absent, exactly one 3-cycle, or otherwise; 3^3-1=26. For k>=3, capture-safe 3-variable recursive path formulas identify exact cycle lengths; k-variable existence tests count distinct cycles through cap k. A permanent cycle-rotation matching game supplies the converse, yielding the minimum-model Euler product. Independently implemented set-based fixed-point tuple refinement for 44 nonempty finite permutation cycle types through 7 vertices: for k=1,2,3 no pairwise mismatch, 3,20,37 observed small-size classes respectively. These finite counts are not the infinite 26-class proof.
